claims.text: This loan costs $3,008.29 in finance charges over 60 months.
In a typical month, what you have left after expenses goes from $900.00 to $474.86.
After the $4,000.00 down payment, your remaining savings of $2,000.00 would cover about 0.60 months of expenses with this loan, down from 2.07 months.
The monthly payment is $375.14, which matches the payment on your contract.
Of the finance charge, $2,508.29 is interest and $500.00 is the prepaid finance charge (a loan fee counted in the finance charge).
Including your down payment, you would pay $26,508.29 in total through this deal.
Recomputing the APR from the amount financed and the payments gives 5.796%, the same as the disclosed APR.
Your savings go from $6,000.00 to $2,000.00 after the down payment.
In this illustrative scenario (an unexpected $2,900.00 expense in month 2), your savings with this loan dip to $49.72 and do not run out.

In this illustrative scenario (no income for 2 months), with this loan your savings run out in month 2 and the unfunded gap reaches $4,975.42; without the loan, savings last all 12 months (lowest point $300.00).
With this loan, your savings could absorb a take-home pay drop of up to 27% for 3 months, or 19% for 6 months, before running out (illustrative).
Each 1 percentage point of interest rate changes the finance charge by about $551.82 (about $9.20 a month) on this loan.
If offered at the same rate, a 48-month term would lower the finance charge by $508.69 and raise the monthly payment by $83.18.
We don't know the lender's buy rate. Ask the dealer whether the 4.75% rate includes a dealer markup.
Debt-to-income isn't shown because we don't have your gross (before-tax) income.
